goal: Move compact block and preferred-download state from CNodeState to Peer
Reduce cs_main lock contention in net_processing by making the fields atomic
reviewability: Merge conflict with master requires rebase

result.summary: Moves m_requested_hb_cmpctblocks, m_provides_cmpctblocks, and fPreferredDownload (renamed to m_preferred_download) from CNodeState to Peer, converting them and the counter m_num_preferred_download_peers into atomics. This eliminates cs_main acquisition across several message processing and block announcement paths in net_processing. It also updates comments in test files referencing the renamed field.
result.problem: Holding the broad cs_main lock to read and write peer-specific compact block flags and download preferences introduces unnecessary locking overhead and tight coupling to legacy node state.

resolved_concerns: dergoegge questioned whether removing cs_main around m_num_preferred_download_peers makes invariants harder to reason about, which was clarified as matching the existing m_wtxid_relay atomic pattern (mzumsande).
mzumsande suggested adding a negative thread-safety annotation (!m_peer_mutex) to NewPoWValidBlock, which the author added.

result.card: This PR moves compact block announcement flags and preferred download status from CNodeState to Peer, converting them and the preferred download counter to atomics. The primary goal is reducing the scope and acquisition of cs_main in net_processing. Several reviewers agree with the direction and the PR has an ACK on the latest commit, but it currently has merge conflicts and needs a rebase before it can proceed.
